newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau on alert as poison enters river.
newsitem.headline: Macau on alert as poison enters river.

text.p: Authorities in Macau said on Tuesday they were monitoring water quality in the territory after a warning from China that a lethal poison had contaminated a nearby river.
Chinese sources in Macau told Reuters that a vehicle carrying potassium cyanide had fallen "recently" into a river in Guangxi province, which flows into the South China Sea, west of Macau.
They also said the contamination, which occurred some 200 km (125 miles) from Macau, would take about three days to reach waters near the Portuguese-administered territory.

But spokesmen for Macau's Urban Council and the Macau Water Supply Company on Tuesday assured the local population that most of Macau's tap water, which comes comes from Zhuhai, in China's southern Guangdong province, was safe.
